name: CALB Group Co., Ltd.
headquarters: No. 1 Jiangdong Avenue, Jintan District, Changzhou, Jiangsu, China
summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** CALB is the fifth-largest energy-storage cell maker in the world on the modal third-party reading and the fourth-largest EV traction battery maker, but it is a challenger in storage and not an incumbent: its 6.8% share sits at roughly a quarter of CATL's, three rivals are clustered within 0.6 percentage points of it, and one serious research house omits it from the top ten altogether. 

**BACKGROUND.** Changzhou-based lithium-ion cell manufacturer listed on HKEX in October 2022 and renamed from CALB Co., Ltd. on 28 December 2022. FY2025 revenue RMB 44.40bn (+60.0%), gross margin 16.69%, profit attributable to owners RMB 1.476bn (+149.6%); H1 2026 revenue RMB 27.08bn (+65.0%) with attributable profit RMB 935.1m, per IFRS accounts filed with HKEX. EV traction is 60.9% of H1 2026 revenue and energy storage 39.1%, the storage half growing faster (+83.8% against +54.8%). The register has no declared controlling shareholder or actual controller: a Changzhou Jintan district concert group holds 26.02% of votes, Xiamen Jinyuan 13.42% and AVIC 9.25%, and the public float is 13.08%. The company was added to the US Department of Defense Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies on 8 June 2026.
ecosystemRole: CALB sits at the cell layer of the storage chain, selling prismatic LFP cells and factory-assembled containers to Chinese state generators, grid companies and system integrators, and prismatic traction cells to seventeen named vehicle programmes. It is one of the four Chinese makers clustered between 6.5% and 7.7% of global storage-cell shipments behind CATL, EVE and Hithium, and unlike its Korean peers it reaches overseas storage demand almost entirely by export rather than by local manufacture: overseas revenue was 2.1% of FY2025 and 4.4% of H1 2026. Its second business, EV traction batteries, is larger and better ranked than its storage business and is what funds the storage capacity build.

productsAndServices.name: ZHIJIU (至久) energy-storage cells
productsAndServices.description: The energy-storage cell brand, one of four battery brands CALB names in its FY2025 results alongside DINGLIU (passenger vehicle), ZHIYUAN (commercial vehicle) and WUJIE (solid-state). Prismatic LFP. Four capacities are in the range: a second-generation 314Ah, a 392Ah, a 588Ah and a 684Ah. The H1 2026 interim states that 314Ah and 392Ah continue in volume delivery while 588Ah and 600+Ah large cells are in mass production. CALB discloses no shipment volume in GWh for this or any other product line, in any period.
highlights: Second-generation 314Ah — described by the company as the first in the industry to reach mass production, with a stated 15,000-cycle life and more than 1,000 cycles of 'zero degradation'
392Ah — positioned by the company as the optimal cell for a 6.25MWh system, on fully line-compatible tooling
588Ah — 3 years zero degradation, 15,000+ cycles, volumetric energy density stated as at least 440 Wh/L on the product page and as 450 Wh/L in the FY2025 results announcement
684Ah — an all-new-generation large-capacity stacked cell, at least 440 Wh/L, supporting more than 6.8MWh in a 20-foot standard container
The 588Ah and 684Ah use thermo-electric separation and dual insulation for safety, with whole-life lithium replenishment cited as the mechanism behind the zero-degradation claim
Cathode chemistry is the company's own LiuJing LFP and a high-manganese LMFP line; no sodium-ion product appears anywhere in CALB's first-party materials
productsAndServices.positioning: CALB names no competitor in any first-party document. Its own FY2025 results claim energy-storage cell shipments ranked fourth globally, without citing a research house. Independent houses do not support fourth on an all-cells basis: SNE Research, TrendForce and InfoLink each place CALB fifth for H1 2026, EVTank placed it sixth for FY2025 and SPIR seventh for H1 2026, while Benchmark Mineral Intelligence omits it from its H1 2026 top ten entirely on a larger stated market. SNE puts CALB 0.1 GWh ahead of REPT BATTERO and 1.3 GWh ahead of Cornex, so the rank is contested rather than held.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Three routes, per the H1 2026 interim: direct to power groups, grid companies and generators; through system integrators and wind and solar developers; and through CALB's own storage-station development, where the company says it is using demonstration projects to open an independent-storage fund investment channel. Overseas sales run through supplier whitelists of regional storage developers and IPPs.
productsAndServices.roadmap: The FY2025 outlook commits to industrialising a 360 Wh/kg high-nickel medium-silicon cylindrical cell and 200+ Wh/kg phosphate-based products, accelerating LMFP, rolling 10Ah-class all-solid-state cells into robotics, and batch-validating a 400 Wh/kg automotive all-solid-state product. A 450 Wh/kg all-solid-state system was reported as developed with first-batch prototype validation complete.

productsAndServices.name: ZHIJIU energy-storage systems — containers, cabinets and residential
productsAndServices.description: Factory-assembled DC blocks built on CALB's own cells, spanning utility-scale containers, commercial and industrial outdoor cabinets, and residential units. CALB appears in no third-party BESS system-integrator ranking: it is named in neither Wood Mackenzie's 2026 global integrator ranking nor Benchmark's H1 2026 system-integrator top ten, so the systems business is a channel for its cells rather than an independently ranked integration business.
highlights: 20-foot 5MWh high-voltage liquid-cooled container — stated volumetric energy up 35%, cycle life up 20%, insert-box-level IP67, system-level immersion water fire suppression, self-consumption down 20%, LCOE down 15%, round-trip efficiency 95%

20-foot 6.25MWh+ high-voltage liquid-cooled container — areal energy density 424 kWh/m2, 8,000+ cycles, DC-side efficiency at least 95%, pack-level IP67, and what the company calls zero newly developed components
314Ah-1P104S liquid-cooled battery box — 1500 V system voltage, 4380 VDC withstand, seismic grade 8, independent per-box cold plate holding maximum temperature spread at or below 3 degrees C

392Ah-1P104S liquid-cooled battery box — dual-row large-module design, pack-level fuse protection, third-generation cell-level thermal barrier and fourth-generation intelligent liquid cooling at 2.5 degrees C spread

Overseas container variant — 22.5% footprint saving, 20-year design life, three-layer cell, pack and container explosion-proof design, key components UL-certified and stated to meet NFPA, UL, IEC and UN standards
Commercial and industrial cabinets at 373 kWh (high-voltage) and 261 kWh (low-voltage), one to ten units in parallel, 350 kW continuous output, 15-year life, scaling from 200 to 5,000 kWh
Residential CJ160F5AA and CJ160F10AA, with the H1 2026 interim widening the range to cover 2.7 kWh to 20 kWh; markets named are Europe, North America and Australia
productsAndServices.positioning: Sold as a route to market for CALB cells rather than as a ranked integrator. The deployment list the company publishes is dominated by Chinese state generators and grid companies, with a small number of large overseas references it does not size in revenue terms.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to generators, grid companies and independent storage funds in China; through developer and IPP supplier whitelists overseas. New commercial models named for 2026 are battery banks and finance leasing.
productsAndServices.roadmap: H1 2026 adds a first Japanese in-front-of-the-meter independent storage project on an ultra-high-voltage node, and 6C high-rate systems for AI data-centre backup. A green-power direct-connect project received first-batch government approval.

productsAndServices.name: DINGLIU (顶流) passenger-vehicle traction batteries
productsAndServices.description: The passenger-car cell and pack line, and CALB's largest business: EV traction was 68.2% of FY2025 revenue and 60.9% of H1 2026. Four sub-lines cover all-climate BEV, super-fast-charge range-extender, high-power plug-in hybrid and high-energy applications. CALB states installed volume ranked fourth globally and third in China for 2025, without naming the source; SNE Research independently places CALB fourth globally in H1 2026 at 31.2 GWh and 5.1%.
highlights: All-climate sub-line — 1,000 km full-charge range, stated zero degradation at minus 20 degrees C, 400 km added in a 5-minute charge
Super-fast-charge sub-line — 10C+ continuous discharge on a 900 V high-voltage platform
High-power sub-line — LFP at 430 Wh/L and LMFP at 480 Wh/L, both described as industry firsts, with discharge above 20C
High-energy sub-line — 220 Wh/kg pack in a 120 kWh+ system, a solid-liquid hybrid at 280 Wh/kg pack, and a 310 Wh/kg R46 cylindrical cell
TPP GEN3.0 no-thermal-propagation architecture combining thermo-electric separation and third-generation aerogel insulation
Seventeen named vehicle programmes including Volvo EX30, smart #1 and #3, Xpeng G6 and X9, SAIC Audi E5 Sportback, GAC Toyota bZ3X, NIO ONVO L90, Lynk & Co 900 and Mazda EZ-6
More than 3,100,000 vehicles fitted across 39 passenger brands and 340+ model applications
productsAndServices.positioning: CALB's stronger and more stable competitive position sits here rather than in storage: SNE has ranked it fourth globally in EV battery installations across FY2025, H1 2026 and January to July 2026, with share rising from 4.4% to 5.1% and growth of 34% to 40%. Gotion's dossier records that CALB passed it in the Chinese ranking during 2026.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to OEMs on model-by-model designated supply, including exclusive designations. Xiaomi Auto publicly named CALB an official power-battery strategic partner on 4 September 2026.
targetSegments: International OEM platforms (Toyota, Volkswagen, Hyundai groups)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Leapmotor A10 and A05 platforms in mass delivery from H2 2026; Huawei HIMA Zhijie RX targeted for H2 2026 delivery.

productsAndServices.name: ZHIYUAN (至远) commercial-vehicle and marine batteries
productsAndServices.description: A modular commercial platform spanning 30 kWh to 900 kWh across vans, micro and light trucks, buses, heavy trucks and construction machinery, plus a marine line. This is CALB's fastest-growing product area by its own reporting: commercial-vehicle shipments rose 225% year on year in H1 2026 after multiple-fold growth in FY2025.
highlights: Heavy commercial standard system — 4C ultra-fast charge, 15-year life, 3,000,000 km stated life, system energy density 167 Wh/kg described as the industry's highest, enclosure volume utilisation at least 94%, 20 to 80% state of charge in 12 minutes
Bus systems warranted to 10 years or 1,000,000 km at 170 Wh/kg and above 260 Wh/L
Marine line — 12,000-cycle life, 3C charge and discharge, energy cells up to 588Ah, pack energy density at least 147 Wh/kg, type-approved by CCS, ABS, Lloyd's Register, Bureau Veritas, RINA and DNV
First to install a 400 Wh/kg solid-liquid hybrid battery in a new-energy commercial vehicle, per the FY2025 results

Named platforms include Xiamen King Long 18m BRT at 427 kWh, Geely Farizon Xingzhi at 101 kWh, Windrose at 705 and 730 kWh, SANY loaders and excavators, and exclusive supply to a UK bus programme where CALB claims the leading NCM share
468 new commercial model certifications in FY2025, up 96%, and 206 more in H1 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: CATL's dossier names CALB as a competitor in commercial-vehicle cells specifically. CALB's China commercial-vehicle installations grew 144.4% in H1 2026 to a stated 9.6% global share of new-energy commercial vehicles, third globally.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to commercial OEMs and machinery makers; new for 2026 are heavy-truck battery swap, battery banks and finance leasing.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Fourth-generation GL-series stacked product for heavy commercial with an in-house CIR integrated architecture, per the H1 2026 interim.

productsAndServices.name: WUJIE (无界) solid-state and emerging applications
productsAndServices.description: The solid-state brand plus the eVTOL, robotics and light-power lines that CALB uses as early adopters for high-energy chemistry. These are pre-scale businesses: CALB reports no revenue for any of them and they are not separately disclosed.
highlights: All-solid-state system developed at 450 Wh/kg with the industry's first batch of prototype validation completed, per the FY2025 results

eVTOL — first-generation flight battery at 300 Wh/kg with 6C charge; second-generation at 360 Wh/kg with stated 200 degrees C solid-liquid hybrid tolerance, aviation-grade fourfold safety redundancy and 1,500+ kW
Robotics — 9-series 4695 cylindrical cells at 310 to 360 Wh/kg and solid-state at 350 to 600 Wh/kg
Light power — LFP at 385+ Wh/L rising to 430+ Wh/L, 10 to 16C discharge, motorcycle range to 700 km
CALB claims the leading industry market share for its R46 310 Wh/kg eVTOL cylindrical cell, without citing a source
productsAndServices.positioning: Positioned as a technology showcase feeding the traction and storage lines rather than as a business in its own right. Named eVTOL customers include XPeng AeroHT, GAC GOVY and Vertaxi.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to eVTOL and robotics developers, and to two-wheeler and light-vehicle makers.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 10Ah-class all-solid-state cells into robotics, and batch validation of a large-capacity 400 Wh/kg automotive all-solid-state product, both named in the FY2025 outlook without a completion date.

recentDevelopments.headline: Hefei Research Institute project signed
recentDevelopments.read: A sixth R&D centre, co-located with the Hefei production base whose minority CALB bought out six weeks earlier — R&D following equity consolidation rather than preceding it.

recentDevelopments.headline: Xiaomi Auto publicly names CALB an official power-battery strategic partner
recentDevelopments.read: The most commercially significant customer event of the period, and it lands while CALB's two largest customers remain unnamed at 16.7% and 15.7% of FY2025 revenue.

recentDevelopments.headline: H1 2026 results: revenue RMB 27.08bn (+65.0%), profit attributable to owners RMB 935.1m (+100.7%)
recentDevelopments.read: Gross margin held at 16.71% while revenue grew two-thirds. Non-controlling interests took 38.6% of profit, a direct consequence of financing production bases as local-government joint ventures.

recentDevelopments.headline: First dividend since listing proposed — interim RMB 0.6 per 10 shares
recentDevelopments.read: After four years of paying nothing, this signals management believes peak capex is passing. It is also proposed while a conversion of 11.69% of the share capital sits unapproved.

recentDevelopments.headline: Bought 12.7230% of the Hefei subsidiary for RMB 690m at the Hefei Equity Exchange, lifting its stake to 42.1082%
recentDevelopments.read: The second local-government minority buy-out in seven months. Together with Wuhan, RMB 1.35bn spent reclaiming earnings that were leaking to non-controlling interests.

recentDevelopments.headline: State Science and Technology Progress Award, second class
recentDevelopments.read: Recorded in the H1 2026 interim. State recognition matters commercially in a market where the buyers are state generators.

recentDevelopments.headline: Added to the US Department of Defense Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies
recentDevelopments.read: The most consequential policy event in the file. Section 805 of the FY2024 NDAA bars Department of War contracting with listed entities from 30 June 2026, and CALB has no US plant and no announced licensing structure to work around it.
recentDevelopments.source: US Department of Defense 1260H update, reported by Holland & Knight and WilmerHale

recentDevelopments.headline: Proposed replacing the H-share auditor RSM Hong Kong with Rongcheng (Hong Kong), the offshore affiliate of CALB's own PRC auditor
recentDevelopments.read: Approved at the 2026-06-09 AGM. The stated rationale is unified audit management; the effect is that the independent second set of eyes on the HK-reported accounts is now an affiliate of the first.

recentDevelopments.headline: Board approves converting 207,102,914 domestic shares (11.69%) into H shares; CSRC filing submitted
recentDevelopments.read: Round three of the H-share full circulation. As at 9 September 2026 it has produced no CSRC acceptance notice, no exchange approval and no completion — see the monthly returns.

recentDevelopments.headline: Bought 8.3155% of the Wuhan subsidiary for RMB 660.08m at the Beijing Equity Exchange, lifting its stake to 59.3155%
recentDevelopments.read: First of the two minority buy-outs. The vendor was a substantial shareholder at subsidiary level, so it was a connected transaction.

recentDevelopments.headline: Completed the acquisition of control of Jiangsu Aoliwei (SZSE: 300507) — board reconstituted, four of five directors CALB-nominated
recentDevelopments.read: CALB became controlling shareholder of a listed auto-parts maker; the target is now formally declared to have no actual controller. A vertical-integration move into pack components and thermal management, bought at the statutory 80% price floor with the seller carrying the downside.

recentDevelopments.headline: Share transfer registered — 87,620,380 Aoliwei shares (10.94%) for RMB 510.83m
recentDevelopments.read: The first of a two-stage completion; the voting-rights waiver over a further 19.55% took effect on 21 October. The RMB 673m share placement that would take CALB to about 22.61% has still not completed.

recentDevelopments.headline: H-share full circulation round two completed — 149,831,290 domestic shares converted
recentDevelopments.read: H shares rose from 611.7m to 761.5m, roughly a quarter added to the float in a day. This is the precedent against which round three's stall is measured.

recentDevelopments.headline: Handan joint venture formed with two Handan municipal state-owned groups — RMB 4.0bn registered capital, CALB 60%
recentDevelopments.read: The template for how CALB finances capacity: local government funds 40%, CALB consolidates, and buys the partner out later once the plant runs.

recentDevelopments.headline: Agreed to acquire control of Jiangsu Aoliwei for RMB 511m plus a voting-rights waiver over 19.55%, with a conditional RMB 673m placement
recentDevelopments.read: Classified as a major transaction under HKEX Chapter 14 and approved at the 2025-07-09 EGM. The seller gave a profit guarantee of RMB 178m for FY2025 and RMB 195m for FY2026, capped at RMB 80m and secured by an RMB 80m deposit.

recentDevelopments.headline: Shares included in the Stock Connect southbound securities list
recentDevelopments.read: Opens mainland institutional and retail flow — a precondition for index inclusion and a partial answer to a 13.08% public float.

recentDevelopments.read: The largest of three CATL claims announced in 26 days. CALB denies infringement in each.

recentDevelopments.headline: CATL sues in the Quanzhou Intermediate People's Court over a battery module utility patent, seeking RMB 60m
recentDevelopments.read: CALB denies infringement and has filed an accepted CNIPA invalidation request against the asserted patent.

recentDevelopments.headline: CATL sues in the Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court over a top-cover assembly patent, seeking RMB 90m
recentDevelopments.read: CALB denies infringement and has filed an accepted CNIPA invalidation request. No progress, settlement or judgment has been announced on any of the three suits in the 21 months since.

recentDevelopments.headline: SNE Research places CALB fifth in global storage-cell shipments for H1 2026 at 31.5 GWh and 6.8%
recentDevelopments.read: 0.1 GWh ahead of REPT and 1.3 GWh ahead of Cornex — a rank held by a margin inside any plausible methodology error.

recentDevelopments.headline: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence publishes an H1 2026 BESS cell ranking that does not name CALB in its top ten
recentDevelopments.read: On a stated market of 490 GWh, 6% larger than SNE's, so this is not a smaller-universe artefact. It is the single largest qualification on any claim that CALB is a top-five storage cell maker.

recentDevelopments.headline: SNE Research places CALB fourth in global EV battery installations for H1 2026 at 31.2 GWh and 5.1%
recentDevelopments.read: The contrast with the storage rank is the dossier's central structural fact: a stable, growing fourth in traction against a contested fifth in storage.

recentDevelopments.headline: 220 MWh energy-storage project signed in Japan
recentDevelopments.read: One of the few overseas orders CALB sizes. Japan is the clearest non-China storage market in its order record.

recentDevelopments.headline: Portuguese state incentives of EUR 350m signed for a EUR 2.067bn, 15 GWh battery plant at Sines
recentDevelopments.read: CALB's only non-PRC plant, with first deliveries targeted for 2027. CALB's own filings name a Portuguese subsidiary but never name Sines, give a capacity or state a date — the detail is third-party.

recentDevelopments.headline: An investor communication record is filed on the company's investor page with every field blank
recentDevelopments.read: Participants, date, venue, attendees and the entire question-and-answer section are empty. A disclosure that discloses nothing, and it is the only investor-communication record published.

relationships.note: Plaintiff against CALB in three patent-infringement suits announced in January 2025, and the storage-cell market leader at roughly four times CALB's share.
relationships.context:
CATL filed three separate patent-infringement claims against CALB that CALB announced on 3 January, 17 January and 28 January 2025 — in the Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court over a secondary-battery top-cover assembly patent seeking RMB 90m, in the Quanzhou Intermediate People's Court over a battery-module utility patent seeking RMB 60m, and in the Hunan High People's Court over a second top-cover patent seeking RMB 110m, RMB 263m in aggregate plus costs.

CALB denies infringement in each and has filed CNIPA invalidation requests against the asserted patents in the first two, both accepted for review. No progress announcement, settlement or judgment has appeared on any of the three in the 21 months since, and CALB reversed its litigation provision in full from RMB 8.155m to nil during FY2025 — a management judgment that the claims will fail.

Separately the two are the extremes of the same market: SNE Research put CATL at 125.0 GWh and 27.1% of global storage-cell shipments for H1 2026 against CALB's 31.5 GWh and 6.8%.

relationships.note: The adjacent rank in storage cells — SNE separates them by 0.1 GWh on an identical 6.8% share.
relationships.context:
SNE Research's H1 2026 global storage-cell table places CALB fifth at 31.5 GWh and REPT BATTERO sixth at 31.4 GWh, both on 6.8% share of a 461.3 GWh market. REPT's own dossier records the same figures and states that fifth and sixth are therefore both defensible for it.

The two are not otherwise commercially linked: no supply, customer or partnership relationship appears in either company's disclosure. They differ in where their storage volume sits — REPT is ranked first globally in residential storage cells by SNE, while CALB's residential line is a small part of a business dominated by utility-scale cells and EV traction.

relationships.note: Direct rival in both markets; Gotion's dossier records that CALB passed it in the Chinese EV battery ranking during 2026.
relationships.context:
The two sit in the same Chinese second tier. On SNE's H1 2026 figures CALB is fourth in global EV battery installations at 31.2 GWh and 5.1% while Gotion is fifth at 28.0 GWh and 4.6%; in storage cells CALB is fifth at 6.8% and Gotion ninth at 4.5%.

Gotion's dossier states that it was passed by CALB in the Chinese ranking during 2026 and places itself in a peer band with CALB and EVE Energy. It also records that CALB, unlike Gotion, is named on the US Department of Defense Section 1260H list — a divergence in policy exposure that this dossier independently confirms.
relationships.scale: 31.2 GWh vs 28.0 GWh EV installs, H1 2026

policyExposure.exposure: CALB Group Co. Ltd. was named on the US Department of Defense's Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies in the update published on 8 June 2026, one of 65 entities added that took the list to 188. Section 805 of the FY2024 NDAA bars the Department of War from entering into, renewing or extending contracts with listed entities for goods, services or technology from 30 June 2026. CALB was added alongside BYD, EVE Energy and NIO; Gotion was not added, and its dossier records that it therefore escapes the Section 805 bans that catch CALB.
policyExposure.mitigation: None stated. CALB has announced no US manufacturing, no licensing structure and no response to the designation in any filing.

policyExposure.exposure: The Section 301 duty on Chinese lithium-ion batteries for non-EV use, which is the grid-storage line, rose from 7.5% to 25% on 1 January 2026, taking the all-in duty on Chinese BESS cells from roughly 37.5% to roughly 55%. CALB's exposure to this is small in revenue terms and large in strategic terms: US revenue was RMB 1.479m in FY2025, effectively nil, having fallen from RMB 50.876m in FY2024.

Foreign-entity-of-concern rules under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act disqualify US projects from tax credits where material assistance from a prohibited foreign entity exceeds a threshold that begins at 55% for construction starting in 2026 and rises to 75% after 2029. Combined with the Section 301 increase and the 1260H listing, the practical position is that CALB has no credible route into the US storage tax-equity market, and its disclosed US revenue is consistent with that.

Carbon-footprint declaration became mandatory for rechargeable industrial batteries placed on the EU market from 18 February 2026, with a digital battery passport carrying provenance, chemistry and recyclability data required for industrial batteries above 2 kWh from February 2027. CALB is one of five Chinese battery makers that explicitly cite EU battery-regulation impact in disclosure, naming recycling-rate and recycled-metal-utilisation requirements. Europe is its fastest-growing overseas region, at RMB 558.6m in H1 2026 against RMB 76.6m a year earlier.
policyExposure.mitigation: CALB holds a Portuguese subsidiary, CALB (EUROPE), S.A., and third-party reporting describes a 15 GWh plant at Sines with first deliveries targeted for 2027 — which would place local production on the battery-passport clock. CALB's own filings name the subsidiary but never name Sines, state a capacity or give a date.

policyExposure.exposure: No source located names CALB on the UFLPA Entity List or reports a CALB-specific detention. The exposure that exists is the rebuttable presumption applying generally to Chinese supply chains rather than anything established as specific to this company. Recorded as not established rather than as absent.

financials.commentary: Reported under IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB, audited by Rongcheng CPA (PRC) and RSM Hong Kong for FY2025; shareholders approved replacing RSM Hong Kong with Rongcheng (Hong Kong), the offshore affiliate of the PRC auditor, at the June 2026 AGM. CALB runs a SINGLE reportable operating segment — the split between EV traction and energy storage below is an IFRS 15 revenue-disaggregation note, and no gross profit, margin or asset split between the two is disclosed anywhere. No analyst consensus is published in a form this dossier could verify: a nine-analyst revenue-revision figure exists only on an aggregator that returned HTTP 403 on three probes, so 'expected' is left empty throughout rather than reconstructed. The company discloses NO shipment or installed volume in GWh for itself, in any period — the only first-party GWh figures are impairment-test sales-volume assumptions per production entity (Jiangsu 36 GWh, Wuhan 38.5 GWh, Chengdu 38 GWh long-run annual), and the headroom on the Jiangsu and Wuhan tests is about 4%.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess CALB is a challenger and not an incumbent in energy-storage cells, and that its incumbent-like position lies in EV traction instead. Basis: SNE Research, TrendForce and InfoLink each rank it fifth globally in H1 2026 storage cells at 31.5 GWh and 6.8%, roughly a quarter of CATL's 27.1%, with REPT 0.1 GWh behind and Cornex 1.3 GWh behind; EVTank ranked it sixth for FY2025 and SPIR seventh for H1 2026. In EV traction the same house ranks it a stable fourth across three consecutive periods with share rising from 4.4% to 5.1%. Two different competitive positions in two different markets, and only the traction one is durable.

2. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess CALB's own claim to fourth place in global storage-cell shipments is scope-shopped and should not be repeated without qualification. Basis: the FY2025 results state 'energy-storage cell shipments ranked fourth globally' and cite no research house; no independent house located supports fourth on an all-cells global basis. The only fourth-place reading available is InfoLink's utility-scale-only sub-metric, a narrower cut than the company's unqualified claim. Confidence is moderate rather than high because CALB may hold a subscription report this dossier could not open.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess the 2026 H-share full circulation has stalled at the CSRC rather than merely being slow, and that this is the most decision-relevant unexplained item in CALB's disclosure record. Basis: the board approved converting 207,102,914 domestic shares on 5 February 2026 and said the filing had been submitted; 216 days later there is no acceptance notice, no exchange approval and no completion. The same company's two prior rounds took 39 days and 122 days to the CSRC notice. Eight consecutive monthly returns through 31 August 2026 show H shares unmoved at 761,499,395 and domestic shares at 1,010,802,463. No announcement states this — it is visible only in the returns.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess the FY2025 and H1 2026 profit inflection is substantially cycle-driven rather than evidence of a widening competitive moat. Basis: gross margin improved just 0.80 points across a year in which revenue rose 60%, and then did not improve at all in H1 2026 (16.71% against 16.69%), while independent commentary attributes the earnings recovery to falling lithium-carbonate input costs and to a storage-cell price recovery that began in late 2025 and lifted the whole sector. A company converting scale into structural advantage would show margin expansion; CALB shows volume expansion at a constant margin.

5. **(High confidence)** We assess CALB is structurally weakest where the storage market is actually growing. Basis: overseas revenue was 2.1% of FY2025 and 4.4% of H1 2026, and US revenue was RMB 1.5m in FY2025, effectively nil. InfoLink reports that non-China shipments were 53.2% of global H1 2026 storage-cell volume, a majority for the first time, and CALB is outside InfoLink's non-China top five having been fourth in that cut for FY2025. Its one non-PRC plant is not due to deliver until 2027.

6. **(High confidence)** We assess the Section 1260H designation of 8 June 2026 forecloses the US market for the foreseeable future and that CALB has published no response to it. Basis: CALB Group Co. Ltd. appears on the Department of Defense list, Section 805 bars Department of War contracting from 30 June 2026, and the Section 301 duty on Chinese non-EV lithium-ion batteries rose to 25% on 1 January 2026. CALB has announced no US plant, no licensing structure and no mitigation in any filing. Its dossier peer Gotion is not listed and its dossier says so explicitly.

7. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess the pattern of local-government joint ventures is now being deliberately unwound at the margin, and that this is where near-term earnings quality improves. Basis: production bases are financed as JVs with municipal investment groups — Handan at RMB 4.0bn registered capital with CALB at 60% is the template — and non-controlling interests took 29.6% of FY2025 profit and 38.6% of H1 2026 profit. CALB then spent RMB 1.35bn in seven months buying minorities out of the Wuhan and Hefei companies through equity-exchange auctions. Reclaiming that leakage is a cheaper source of attributable earnings growth than margin expansion.

8. **(Low confidence)** Trade press reports a EUR 2.067bn, 15 GWh CALB plant at Sines, Portugal, with EUR 350m of state incentives and first deliveries in 2027. CALB's own filings name a Portuguese subsidiary, CALB (EUROPE), S.A., and describe a European industrial base as established, but never name Sines, state a capacity or give a date. Treat the Sines specifics as third-party and unconfirmed by the company.

**Collection gap:** CALB discloses no shipment or installed volume in GWh for itself in any period, and no gross margin, profit or asset split between EV traction and energy storage, because it reports a single operating segment. Every GWh figure in this dossier is therefore a third-party estimate. No published analyst consensus was verifiable — the one aggregator carrying nine-analyst revision figures returned HTTP 403 on three probes — so all 'expected' fields are left empty. CALB names no competitor anywhere in its own materials, and publishes no photographs of any director or executive.

**Collection gap:** the three CATL patent suits announced in January 2025, claiming RMB 263m in aggregate, have produced no progress announcement, settlement or judgment in 21 months, and CALB reversed its litigation provision in full to nil during FY2025. Chinese secondary sources describe a wider docket of eight suits and roughly RMB 700m claimed, plus RMB 1.007bn counterclaimed by CALB; none of that is in CALB's own filings and this dossier does not adopt it.

- *A CSRC acceptance notice for the 207,102,914-share conversion:* arrival would show the stall was administrative; continued silence past the one-year mark in February 2027 would indicate the filing has failed. The monthly returns are the tell, not the announcements.

- *Completion of the RMB 673m Jiangsu Aoliwei placement:* the long-stop under the share transfer agreement runs to roughly 6 November 2026. Completion lifts CALB from 10.94% to about 22.61%; lapse would leave it a 10.94% controlling shareholder of a company with no actual controller.
- *Any judgment or settlement in the CATL suits:* a first adverse ruling against a nil provision would be a direct earnings event and would test the FY2025 reversal.

- *H1 2027 overseas revenue:* the Sines plant is due to deliver from 2027. Overseas revenue crossing into double-digit percentage would confirm the export-to-local-manufacture transition; another year near 4% would mean it has not started.
- *Gross margin in the FY2026 results:* a second consecutive period at about 16.7% on another 60% revenue increase would confirm judgment 4; expansion above 18% would weaken it.

- *Whether the interim dividend is paid and repeated:* the first distribution since the 2022 listing, proposed 28 August 2026. A repeat at the full year would corroborate the peak-capex reading; a one-off would not.
